label: culture-variety-pilot-factcheck-codex-20261012
review_type: independent two-item source, option-quality, and duplicate review

scope.blindness: No full-blind claim: the lead had already read the key/article material before this review.

batch_verdict.reason: The pilot has useful non-award culture premises and no released-bank semantic duplicate found, but both items need precise wording or option repair before acceptance.

duplicate_check.method: Searched current quizzes/**/*.json for Волшебник страны Оз, Dorothy, ruby slippers, Джими Хендрикс, Hendrix, and электрогитар.
duplicate_check.result: Wizard of Oz hits concern Toto's breed and Judy Garland/Dorothy; no slipper adaptation item was found. No Hendrix/instrument item was found. These are not semantic duplicates of the pilot objectives.

items.key_and_options: PASS — silver is the correct book answer; four one-word color options are distinct, parallel, and have no length giveaway.
sources_and_claims: Library of Congress says Baum's slippers were originally silver; the displayed 1939 pair has red satin and 2,300 sequins on each shoe, while earlier designs included one reminiscent of silver shoes.
AFI confirms silver footwear in Baum's books and describes the sepia beginning/end and transition to color on arrival in Oz.
The LOC wording is qualified: the slippers were 'purportedly' changed to ruby to take full advantage of color photography. The draft states this as definite causality.
items.required_correction: Change 'Смена цвета помогла показать возможности цветной съёмки Technicolor' to a qualified formulation, for example: 'По версии Библиотеки Конгресса, цвет, вероятно, выбрали, чтобы использовать возможности цветной съёмки.' Restrict the red-satin/2,300-sequin wording to the exhibited pair or state that this is how the documented shoes were made.

items.key_and_options: Core answer is supported, but it is conspicuously longer and the other three options are implausible/absurd (pick thickness, fourth pickup, removal of all frets). This gives the answer away.
sources_and_claims: Fender describes Hendrix as a left-handed player using an upside-down, reverse-strung right-handed guitar and separately says he flipped right-handed guitars.
Experience Hendrix/Museum of Pop Culture says Izabella's strings and bone nut were reversed, the strap pin moved, and the guitar played upside-down; it identifies the instrument at Woodstock in 1969.
Fender's artist article supports the Monterey 1967 and Woodstock 1969 references.
The draft's 'замену верхнего порожка' is inaccurate: the cited source says the bone nut was reversed, not replaced.
items.required_correction: Replace 'замену верхнего порожка' with 'переворачивание верхнего порожка' or 'смену его ориентации'. Use parallel, plausible options, for example: (A) 'Переворачивал корпус и менял порядок струн' [correct]; (B) 'Менял верхний порожек, не переворачивая корпус'; (C) 'Переставлял крепление ремня, не меняя струн'; (D) 'Переворачивал корпус, сохраняя порядок струн'.

limitations: Review is limited to these two frozen items and their five supplied citations; it does not make a claim about a wider culture bank.
The Library of Congress gives the 2,300-sequin detail for the pair it describes, so it does not independently establish an all-production-pairs claim.
No canonical, source, build, SSH, publication, or writer-file change was made.
required_next_gate: Apply the two concrete repairs and obtain a fresh independent review before any acceptance or publication decision.
